newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka expects 12 pct '97 net increase.
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka expects 12 pct '97 net increase.

text.p: Croatia's leading Zagrebacka Banka expects 1997 net profit for the parent bank to be 12 percent higher than last year, chief executive officer Franjo Lukovic said on Tuesday.
"The 1997 business plan foresees a 17 percent growth in the bank's balance sheet and a 12 percent growth in profit after tax," Lukovic told the annual shareholders meeting.
He stressed the bank's performance would not suffer despite an increase in the corporate profit tax rate to 35 from 25 percent, which came into effect a few months ago.

Zagrebacka's shareholders approved a dividend of six German marks per ordinary share on the bank's 1996 net profit of 219 million kuna. The dividend payout will total 69 million kuna, while the rest will be channelled into reserves.
"The value of total shareholders' funds was also boosted by the 156 million kuna in capital reserves that was created this way," Lukovic said.
He made no forecast for the 1997 dividend. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
